OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and allows only secure second factors (TOTP, security keys/passkeys, GitHub Mobile; no SMS), so no account can read or change a repository's sensitive settings without MFA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: The organization's base permission is read, so a new member or collaborator gets read access until an owner grants more by hand; every elevated grant (the three owners' admin) is an explicit assignment. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main; its only bypass actor (the maintainer) holds it in pull_request mode, which excuses the review while merging a pull request and never a direct push, so a direct push to main is refused for everyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset carries a deletion rule (plus non_fast_forward) with no bypass actor, and classic protection sets allow_deletions false, so main cannot be deleted by anyone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at both the organization and the repository, and GitHub Actions cannot approve pull requests; every workflow also declares permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top and elevates per job only for what that job does (id-token for publishing and attesting, attestations, security-events for CodeQL/Scorecard, contents: write only in the release job); zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run; untrusted event fields and dispatch inputs reach run: steps only through env: variables, never interpolated into a script, and zizmor's template-injection audit runs in the required lint check to refuse the unsafe form. The review bot's mention job is also switched off by the CLAUDE_REVIEW_ENABLED variable. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request trigger, which gives a fork's code no secrets and a read-only token; the one job holding a secret on a pull request (the review) runs only when the head repository is this repository, and the comment-triggered job checks out the default branch, not the pull request's code. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: Collaborator input reaches pipelines as workflow_dispatch inputs, which are passed to steps through env: rather than interpolated into scripts (zizmor's template-injection audit enforces it) and checked by the step that consumes them, e.g. pypi-install.yml waits for the index to serve exactly the version named. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/pypi-install.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D) set by a signed v* tag; release.yml's version-check job refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: sdist, wheel, <name>-<version>.cdx.json and <tag>.intoto.jsonl (<tag>.attestation.jsonl for v2026.9.29). The attestation binds each to its digest.

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-mnemonics.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS-only; PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle, so a tampered download fails verification. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-mnemonics/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: Every release carries CHANGELOG.md's entry (every change) and RELEASE_NOTES.md's (what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included); the GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Build and release pipelines take dependencies only through uv from PyPI, run with --locked against the committed uv.lock, and actions are pinned by commit SHA (enforced by the organization's sha_pinning_required). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 Sigstore attestation from Trusted Publishing, and the GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle, <tag>.intoto.jsonl (v2026.9.29 keeps the name <tag>.attestation.jsonl). The tag itself is signed, and the tag-integrity ruleset requires that.

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and its push protection are enabled, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused; the detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run against .secrets.baseline in the required lint check for credentials GitHub does not recognise. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: The organization's policy, https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2913-L2940 : a secret is an environment secret that only the owners can reach, any other store's entry is recorded in the spending repository's REPOSITORY.md, a secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected, and the list is reviewed yearly in a "Secrets review <year>" issue. tests/secrets_test.py reads every store and refuses an unrecorded entry.

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is README.md's first-use section, which tests/readme_test.py runs, plus the API reference rendered from the docstrings, published at https://btclib-mnemonics.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report issue form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for what a report needs; SECURITY.md routes a vulnerability away from the public tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md and RELEASING.md give the gh attestation verify command (with --repo and --signer-workflow, or --bundle offline) for the release assets, and RELEASING.md gives the rebuild-from-tag check that reproduces the sdist. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verification command pins the repository, the signer workflow (reusable-build.yml, and reusable-attest.yml for releases before v2026.10.2) and the tag with --source-ref. An attestation from any other workflow or repository is refused: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions* states that a release stops receiving security updates as soon as the next one is published, since only the latest is supported and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: Each runtime dependency's reason is written beside it in pyproject.toml; dependencies are obtained from PyPI through uv and pinned in uv.lock, and tracked by Dependabot's weekly grouped updates with a seven-day cooldown, as the standard's sections 1 and 11 state. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md names who holds access to sensitive resources: the maintainer (the only bypass actor) and the three owners, each an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments, with the command that reads them back; the tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: an issue first, one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what an acceptable contribution meets: an issue behind it, one subject, the lint gate (ruff select ALL, strict mypy), line and branch coverage at 100%, a signed commit, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/GOVERNANCE.md#L44-L46 : a grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there.

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off status check, so a pull request cannot merge unless every commit carries a Signed-off-by: trailer (the DCO assertion) from its author. Commits made in the web interface are signed off automatically (web_commit_signoff_required is on). https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-mnemonics/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: The release is pure Python, with nothing compiled; even so, every release attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM (<name>-<version>.cdx.json) generated from the built wheel, listing both files' SHA-256, the license and the declared dependencies, and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: Classic protection on main requires the listed status checks with strict up-to-date; enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge that lands without them is a manual bypass, which is the case the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: The project has no additional subproject repository: each release is built from this one repository, and the package has no dependencies.

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary file is docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, a copy of Python's documentation inventory, and check-added-large-files keeps builds out of the tree.

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: No executable, library or similar binary artifact is committed. The only binary file is data: docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, a copy of Python's intersphinx inventory used by the documentation build.

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') runs the test suite on every pull request and is a required status check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The documented policy is 100% line and branch coverage (standard section 8; CONTRIBUTING.md), so a change adding untested functionality fails the required test check; pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires an approval from somebody other than the author and limits the maintainer's bypass to emergencies, since 2026-10-03. The ruleset's bypass actor can still merge without one, and every pull request so far was merged by its author.

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: CLAUDE.md's *Architecture* section documents the components, their layering and every place the software reaches outside the process, and ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Trust boundaries* and *Threat model* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#architecture

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://btclib-mnemonics.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module (ruff's D rules require them, and a docs test fails when a shipped module is missing from the reference); CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states what is public.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting channels and states the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L19

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org, which reaches the three organization owners. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on the repository (a CVE can be requested from them), which SECURITY.md commits to; none has been needed yet. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3120-L3135 : the CycloneDX SBOM published with each release carries a vulnerabilities array, built from the tree's .github/vex.toml, with analysis.state not_affected, a CycloneDX justification and the reason for each vulnerability judged not to affect the release. No vulnerability is judged so today, so no tree keeps the file; the alignment suite (tests/vex_test.py) refuses a Dependabot alert dismissed as not affecting without its entry.

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909 : every pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action, which fails on an added or changed dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml, and an exception is a purl named there with its reason.

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3149-L3160 : release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares before any publish job, and an advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id the release's own signed VEX document states as not affecting it.

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: Every pull request runs the Dependency review job (policy: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909), and the job is a required status check on main ("lint / Dependency review" in branch protection), so a pull request that violates the policy cannot merge.

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets the threshold at zero: ruff runs select = ALL (bandit's S rules included), and every finding is fixed or suppressed with a # noqa and a reason at its site; zizmor holds workflows to the same. CodeQL alerts have no stated threshold. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the bandit S rules, strict mypy, zizmor on workflows, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding unless suppressed in place with a reason; CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization has three owners, each an administrator of this repository -- fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, confirmed live via `gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/collaborators` -- so the loss of any one leaves two who can create and close issues, accept changes and cut a release; GOVERNANCE.md's *Continuity* states that every owner is an administrator of every repository, its rules and publishing environments included. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: btclib-mnemonics is a library with no user interface: no CLI, no GUI and no web front end, so accessibility best practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md gives the threat model (what is defended, the adversaries, what is not defended), the trust boundaries, the secure design principles and the common implementation weaknesses with what counters each, naming the file, test or workflow behind every argument. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the test suite, on every supported interpreter, on every push to main and every pull request, and its aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: Pure-Python source is used directly (uv_build, no compilation step), so there is nothing whose bit-for-bit regeneration to test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by .github/scripts/normalize_sdist.py; sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release from its signed tag and verifies it against the release's build-provenance attestation, and passed on v2026.9.29 (run 36620125716). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: Most commits are the maintainer's: 42 of 43 non-bot commits, with one outside contribution. Continuity rests on the three organization owners GOVERNANCE.md names, each an administrator of this repository.

code_of_conduct.justification: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md lives in btclib-org/.github and is shown by GitHub as this repository's code of conduct through the organization's default community-health-file inheritance, confirmed via the repository's community-profile API. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff.lint] selects every ruff rule family (`select = ["ALL"]`) with a documented `ignore` list, and [tool.mypy] runs in strict mode; CONTRIBUTING.md names both and the commands that enforce them on every contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the public-surface, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: One outside contributor so far, in https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/pull/28; there are not yet two significant unassociated contributors. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/graphs/contributors

copyright_per_file.justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", and ruff's flake8-copyright rule (CPY001) keeps it there, e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/src/btclib_mnemonics/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: The algorithms are fixed by the specifications the package implements -- a BIP39, SLIP-0039 or Electrum sentence has to stretch to the seed every other implementation computes -- so there is no alternative algorithm a user could switch to without leaving the standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: Every primitive is called from the standard library -- hashlib's sha256, sha512 and pbkdf2_hmac, hmac, secrets and os.urandom -- and none is reimplemented. What the package writes itself is only what the specifications define above those primitives: SLIP-0039's GF(256) interpolation and its Feistel structure, and the mnemonic encodings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: btclib-mnemonics performs no network communications -- nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib -- and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics

crypto_credential_agility.justification: btclib-mnemonics is a library with no configuration file or credential store: entropy, mnemonics, passphrases and shares are caller-supplied function parameters, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

crypto_floss.justification: no closed source dependencies: the standard library alone

crypto_keylength.justification: Every default meets 112 bits: bip39.mnemonic_from_entropy draws 128 bits when given none, electrum's generator draws 132 bits rounded up to whole words, and slip39 refuses a master secret under 128 bits. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics

crypto_password_storage.justification: does not store passwords: a passphrase is stretched into a seed and handed back, never stored or used to authenticate anyone

crypto_pfs.justification: implements no network key-agreement protocol: the package performs no network communications at all

crypto_published.justification: Every mechanism is a published one: BIP39 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, SHA-256 checksum), SLIP-0039 (Shamir sharing over GF(256), an HMAC-SHA256 digest share, a four-round Feistel network whose round function is PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256) and Electrum's seed schemes (HMAC-SHA512 version prefix, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, and the pre-2.0 iterated SHA-256), each checked against the vectors its authors publish. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/README.md

crypto_random.justification: Every random draw comes from the operating system's CSPRNG: secrets for BIP39's and Electrum's default entropy and the simulated dice, os.urandom as the default entropy_source of SLIP-0039's splitting; nothing under src/ uses the random module, which ruff's S311 flags there. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

crypto_tls12.justification: btclib-mnemonics performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics

crypto_used_network.justification: btclib-mnemonics does not talk to the network at all -- it opens no socket, runs no subprocess and writes no file, as ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* states, and no test reaches the network, as CONTRIBUTING.md states -- so there are no network communications for a secure-protocol choice to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

crypto_verification_private.justification: btclib-mnemonics performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics

crypto_weaknesses.justification: No SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/: the hashes are SHA-256 and SHA-512, alone, in HMAC or in PBKDF2, with the iteration counts the specifications fix (BIP39's and Electrum's 2048, SLIP-0039's 10000 * 2^e, the pre-2.0 Electrum scheme's 100000). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics

dco.justification: Every commit carries a Signed-off-by: trailer from its author (the DCO assertion): main requires the lint / Sign-off status check, which refuses a pull request with a commit lacking it, and CONTRIBUTING.md says so. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

delivery_mitm.justification: Distribution channels use HTTPS exclusively: GitHub, and PyPI through Trusted Publishing. [osps_br_03_02]

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot's version updates are configured in .github/dependabot.yml for the github-actions, uv and docker ecosystems, dependabot_security_updates is enabled on the repository, and CodeQL and OpenSSF Scorecard run on a schedule as well. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md links the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges on the lines the organization standard reserves for them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: CLAUDE.md's *Architecture* section documents the layers bottom-up (exceptions and _utils, entropy and mnemonic, the three schemes bip39, electrum and slip39, none importing another, and dispatch above them), that the package imports nothing outside the standard library, and that it stops at the seed. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#architecture

documentation_basics.justification: README.md says what the package holds and what it does not, how to install it, and gives a first use that tests/readme_test.py runs; CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md and ASSURANCE_CASE.md cover the rest. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/README.md

documentation_current.justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page, and tests/readme_test.py runs every Python block of README.md, so neither the reference generated from the docstrings nor the README's example can drift from the code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_interface.justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference published at https://btclib-mnemonics.readthedocs.io/; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them.

documentation_quick_start.justification: README.md's *A seed from a mnemonic, and a secret split into shares* is a first use -- a BIP39 sentence from entropy, its seed, its scheme recognized, and a SLIP-0039 2-of-3 split recombined -- and tests/readme_test.py runs it, so it is the one the suite checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/README.md

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, covers the period until 2027-09-30, is reviewed every September, and states what is intended and what is deliberately not; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* states what a user cannot expect -- no zeroization of secret material, nothing constant-time, randomness from the operating system, the interactive dice collector -- and ASSURANCE_CASE.md argues why what it does claim holds. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis.justification: mutation testing and fuzzing (ClusterFuzzLite over every decoder, and Hypothesis in tests/fuzz_test.py): https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/mutation.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

enhancement_responses.justification: Contributions are answered and merged: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/pull/28, an outside contributor's fix, was merged the day it was opened.

external_dependencies.justification: pyproject.toml declares `dependencies = []` -- the package imports the standard library alone, which tests/imports_test.py asserts of every module -- and the test and tooling dependencies in its dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: The project site https://btclib.org/btclib-mnemonics/ is served over HTTPS behind Cloudflare and answers Content-Security-Policy (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security; check with curl -sI https://btclib.org/btclib-mnemonics/

hardening.justification: ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the flake8-bandit (S) family, so a hardening-relevant defect -- an unsafe deserialization, a weak random call, a shell injection -- is caught at the lint gate rather than only in review; CodeQL runs the same search at a different granularity on every push. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles one by one -- economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, open design, least privilege, psychological acceptability -- each to the file or test that carries it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with a BTClibMnemonicsTypeError or BTClibMnemonicsValueError, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* requires; tests/input_validation_test.py drives the rule over every public function, and tests/fuzz_test.py holds every decoder to it on hostile sentences. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_common.justification: `python -m pip install --upgrade btclib-mnemonics` installs it from PyPI, as README.md says, and pypi-install.yml installs the published version on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows after each release and weekly. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-mnemonics/

installation_development_quick.justification: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command, uv being the only tool to install first; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP (pyupgrade) and FA rule families run at `select = ["ALL"]` and flag deprecated stdlib and typing constructs; the deps-latest and deps-oldest sentinels exercise the supported interpreter range weekly, so a newly deprecated API is caught close to its deprecation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: The text the package produces for end users is the mnemonic sentence itself, and it produces it in every language the specifications define word lists for: the twelve word lists of BIP39's reference implementation (Japanese joined by the ideographic space BIP39 requires) and Electrum's own; the language is read back off the words. SLIP-0039 defines English alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tree/main/src/btclib_mnemonics/_data

know_common_errors.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md lists the common implementation weaknesses, such as CWE-209 and CWE-330, and what counters each: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

know_secure_design.justification: The maintainer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md, which applies Saltzer and Schroeder's principles to the code one by one. It was reviewed by another owner in https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26.

license_location.justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/LICENSE>.

license_per_file.justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/src/btclib_mnemonics/__init__.py

maintained.justification: The repository was created on 2026-09-29 and is under active development: its CI, CodeQL, fuzzing and mutation workflows ran that day, and Dependabot's first update pull requests were handled the same day. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported, per SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*; the upgrade path is documented instead -- RELEASING.md requires a breaking-changes check (`griffe check`) against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md carries what a user has to act on, the first release's already listing the migration from btclib_wallet.mnemonic name by name. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

no_leaked_credentials.justification: detect-secrets baseline gated by pre-commit, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection enabled on the repository: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

regression_tests_added50.justification: Every bug fixed so far came with a test in the same pull request, for example https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/pull/39 and https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/pull/41. The 100% coverage gate and CONTRIBUTING.md keep that so.

release_notes.justification: RELEASE_NOTES.md carries each release's human-readable notes, and release.yml publishes the tag's section as the GitHub release's text: v2026.9.29's lists the migration from btclib_wallet.mnemonic name by name. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/releases/tag/v2026.9.29

release_notes_vulns.justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability that had a CVE, and the repository has no security advisories. v2026.10.2 fixed findings of an internal security review, none with a CVE: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26.

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: Bugs are reported on the GitHub issue tracker, through the issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, as CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* describes: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues>. Vulnerabilities go through SECURITY.md instead: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md>.

report_responses.justification: Bug reports are answered the day they are filed: issues #15 to #24 of 2026-09-30 were each closed by a fix within 3 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed

report_tracker.justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member (organization setting two_factor_requirement_enabled = true), so nobody without 2FA can change a repository. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* section names the maintainer, the owners, repository administrators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot and Dependabot, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and has 'Only allow secure two-factor methods' selected, which refuses SMS as a second factor: only TOTP apps, security keys/passkeys and GitHub Mobile are accepted. Read from the organization's security settings on 2026-09-30 and recorded at https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: Security review of 2026-09-30 by pmazzocchi, an owner of the organization other than the maintainer: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26 . It pins its scope to a commit, checks every claim and trust boundary of ASSURANCE_CASE.md (the security requirements and boundary, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md), states what it did not cover, and files each finding as an issue.

signed_releases.justification: v2026.10.2 is on PyPI through Trusted Publishing with PEP 740 attestations, and its GitHub release carries a Sigstore provenance bundle, v2026.10.2.intoto.jsonl. SECURITY.md gives the `gh attestation verify` command that checks it: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

sites_password_security.justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; this repository runs no site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: No open issue carries the label "good first issue" today (2026-10-03). Small, self-contained issues get the label when they turn up: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1541

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule, on every pull request and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules, both FLOSS static-analysis tools looking for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_often.justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification:
https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/test.yml
The test suite covers the whole code base, a 100% line-and-branch floor the build enforces, and it answers to vectors their authors publish: BIP39's reference implementation's and the Japanese ones BIP39 cites, SLIP-0039's own, and Electrum's. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to the upstream commit it was copied from, and says whether the two still match.

test_branch_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets branch = true under [tool.coverage.run], and the 100% fail_under gate includes branches: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_continuous_integration.justification: test.yml runs on every pull request and every push to main, and its aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check on main. Its runs on main are listed at https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/actions/workflows/test.yml

test_policy_mandated.justification: The 100% coverage floor described in CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* is an enforced written policy: a line or branch of new functionality with no covering test fails the CI gate outright, `fail_under = 100.0` admitting no exception. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 100.0`, gated on every pull request by the required test.yml; the suite is gated well above the 80% floor this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 under [tool.coverage.report], and the required test check enforces it on every pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100%-coverage gate as part of how a change is proposed, which states the policy this criterion asks for: new functionality is not accepted without a covering test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires an approval from somebody other than the author and limits the maintainer's bypass to emergencies, since 2026-10-03. Every pull request so far was merged by its author, and the ruleset's bypass actor can still do so: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

updateable_reused_components.justification: At runtime the package reuses only the standard library. The test and tooling components are PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel runs the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml

version_semver.justification: CalVer, YYYY.M.D, declared in pyproject.toml and explained in RELEASE_NOTES.md: the number says when a release was cut and promises nothing about compatibility, so a breaking change is announced in RELEASE_NOTES.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

version_tags.justification: Each release is tagged v<version> on the release commit, as RELEASING.md requires: v2026.9.29. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/tags

version_tags_signed.justification: Release tags are signed (git tag -s), and the tag-integrity ruleset's required_signatures rule on refs/tags/v* refuses an unsigned one at the forge; v2026.9.29's signature verifies. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/RELEASING.md

version_unique.justification: Each release carries a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, declared once in pyproject.toml and tagged v<version>; the first is 2026.9.29. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/releases/tag/v2026.9.29

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: Ten findings of the 2026-09-30 security review were filed publicly and fixed in v2026.10.2, within 3 days. No security advisory exists: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26.

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: Ten findings of the 2026-09-30 security review were filed publicly and fixed in v2026.10.2, within 3 days. No security advisory exists: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26.

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: The findings of the 2026-09-30 security review, all resolved, are credited to the reviewer, pmazzocchi, in SECURITY.md and in https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26.

vulnerability_report_response.justification: The findings of the 2026-09-30 security review were answered and fixed within 3 days: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/issues/26. No report has reached the private channel.

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* section documents the private channel (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see it, and how a CVE can be requested; private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository (`gh api repos/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/private-vulnerability-reporting` answers enabled). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: warning are not tolerated: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again by the required lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-mnemonics/blob/main/pyproject.toml
